key_insight: VISTA fixes GRPO’s “all-success/all-failure” problem for GUI grounding by comparing rollouts across multiple target-preserving views of the same screen, making relative learning informative again.
engineering_relevance: The method improves robustness of GUI agents under view changes and is directly useful for training grounding models that must locate interface elements reliably across cropped or shifted screenshots.
method: Builds each GRPO comparison group from multiple cropped views that still preserve the target element and remap its box exactly.
Adds a self-verified cross-view anchor trained with advantage-weighted loss, but only when the model already achieves a maximum-reward rollout.
Keeps reinforcement learning from collapsing into pure imitation by excluding the anchor from the group baseline.
evidence_signal: Across five GUI-grounding benchmarks and multiple Qwen backbones, VISTA improves accuracy; on ScreenSpot-Pro, Qwen3-VL 4B/8B/30B-A3B rises from 55.5/52.7/53.7 to 63.4/65.8/67.0.
watch_item: Performance depends on constructing valid target-preserving crops and exact box remapping, which may be tricky for complex interfaces or tightly packed elements.
paper_title: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
